name: Partenavia P.68 / Vulcanair P.68
summary: Italian six-seat high-wing twin built since 1970, used for light transport, training and observation work; the Observer has a glazed nose.

engines: Two Lycoming engines in slim nacelles on the wing
fuselage: Slim cabin with large flat side windows
Long, pointed nose (glazed on the Observer)
Fixed tricycle gear in small pod-like fairings on most
tail: Tall, angular fin with a large, boxy horizontal tail

tellTales: High-wing light twin with a long, sharply pointed nose
No wing struts, with fixed gear in small pods
Tall angular fin with a boxy horizontal tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The Islander is blockier with a rectangular cabin and a blunter nose; the P.68 is slimmer with a long pointed nose.
The P2006T is smaller with a rounded nose and retractable gear; the P.68 is a larger six-seater with fixed gear.
The P2012 has a row of large round windows and a rounded nose; the P.68 has flat rectangular windows and a long pointed nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
